summary.intent: Run WP Q (Session 4) from the launch plan: build a `just verify-real` rehearsal harness that exercises release recovery against local registries through production binding. Then, per the lead's follow-up, add named Cargo registries as a `publish-to` target (separate PR) so Cargo can be rehearsed too.
summary.outcome: WP Q was pushed as PR #572 with 5 passing npm/PyPI rehearsals and all gates green, no production code changes, and no Cargo rehearsal. The named-Cargo-registry feature was implemented test-first in a new worktree, gates passed, and it is committed (signed) but not yet pushed; mutants, the fresh Opus reviewer, changeset, trail linking and the follow-up Cargo rehearsals plus native matrix remain.

repo: Registry https rule: `canonical_registry_url` accepts https on loopback but rejects http even on loopback, so local registries must serve self-signed TLS to bind through production code with no test-only allowance.

callisto opens no sockets itself; all registry traffic goes via child processes (npm, curl, twine, cargo) that inherit the environment, so NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, CURL_CA_BUNDLE and REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE carry the trust anchor.

pypiserver cannot serve the PEP 691 JSON simple index that callisto's PyPI observation requires, and it 303-redirects unknown packages unless `disable_fallback=True`; the harness uses a small stdlib JSON index server for the index side and pypiserver for uploads.

Source replacement in cargo config does not redirect `cargo publish`; with `--registry crates-io` it hits the real crates.io API (the probe got a 401). That is why Cargo could not be rehearsed until named registries existed.
`PublishTarget` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so a forgotten cross-crate match arm compiles and fails at runtime via `_ => UnsupportedRelease` in derive.rs; boundary tests must cover it.

Conflicting-tag scenario: callisto publishes and tags the dependency package before it reaches the dependent's tag conflict, so the test asserts E167 and a foreign tag untouched, not 'nothing published'.
Tool pins live in `.github/actions/install-registry-test-tools/action.yml`; the action now delegates to `just verify-real-tools`, which installs into `target/verify-real/`.

Named Cargo registry design: add a `PublishTarget::CargoRegistry { name }` variant, validate at load in `parse_publish_target` against `[registries]`, reuse E330 for unknown or non-cargo names, and E336 still rejects a url on cargo registries. `config_str()` changes from `&'static str` to `&str`.

code.finding: `parse_publish_target` only knew `crates-io`; it now takes `&registries` and resolves cargo-kind registry names.
Cross-crate match on non-exhaustive `PublishTarget` ends in `#[allow(unreachable_patterns)] _ => UnsupportedRelease`; the fingerprint arm must include `CargoRegistry`.
Site for the new `CargoRegistry` variant; the `registry_key`, `ecosystem`, `config_str`, `registry_override` and `is_implemented` methods all need updating.
Publish argv already passes `--registry <key>` for any key other than `cratesIo`, and `cargo_registry_name` passes keys through.
Existing test `red_d01_every_cargo_info_observation_names_a_registry_explicitly` is the model for the new named-registry boundary tests.

workflow: Run long gate sequences from a script that writes its own output file, because the sandbox guard rejects redirect forms.
Write boundary tests first and confirm they are red before implementing.
Use explicit-refspec pushes (`HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>`), verify with `git ls-remote`, and sign commits without session trailers.
Subagent hand-back messages carry no user authority; design reports were treated as advice and only the user's instructions as approval.
Spike risky tooling (TLS handling in curl, twine, pypiserver) before building the harness around it.

friction: Network fetch failed in the sandbox and had to be retried unsandboxed.
Greedy Python string replacements broke the old e2e test file (`curl_get` call sites and a delimiter), which only surfaced when the gates failed to compile.
macOS python venv setup failed, so the venv was recreated with `uv`, and `--seed` was later needed.
The first PyPI test run failed twice: pypiserver redirected on fallback and could not serve the JSON index.
The Cargo rehearsal attempt hit real crates.io with a fake token before it was clear source replacement does not redirect publish.
The delayed-visibility test was flaky in design (non-atomic file copy, possibly equal ports), fixed with an atomic rename, distinct ports and a log assertion.
open_items: Push the named-cargo-registries commit with an explicit refspec and verify with `git ls-remote`.
Run mutation testing on the production diff and a fresh Opus reviewer; add the `callisto add` changeset (callisto-cli:minor); link trail #460; update docs/publishing.md:38 and docs/config.md.

After that PR merges, add Cargo rehearsals (partial publish adopted on rerun, delayed visibility, conflicting tag) to #572 against a local sparse registry, and update the AGENTS.md and release.md lines that say Cargo cannot be rehearsed.
Record the native install/load matrix from `native_resolution_e2e_tests`, which is missing from #572.
Owner decisions: reject `publish-to = ["cratesIo"]` with E330 as proposed, and a dead `[registries.crates-io] kind = "cargo"` entry left as a follow-up.
`config_str()` returning `&str` is a semver-visible API change in the MIT `callisto-model` crate.
Real `cargo info --registry <name>` against an actual alternative registry is unproven until the verify-real Cargo rehearsal exists.
After #572 merges, remove the verify-real worktree and its local branch.
Not run for #572: `just ci` and the CI action change on a real runner.
